test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Hardly had I started mowing the lawn that) it started raining.

options.text: No sooner did I started mowing the lawn than
Hardly had I started mowing the lawn when
Hardly did I start mowing the lawn than

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3' **i.e**. 'Hardly had I started mowing the lawn when'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses the structure **"Hardly had I started... that,**" which **is incorrect.**
 
• The **correct structure **to express the idea of one event happening immediately after another is **"Hardly had I started... when."**
 
• The corrected form of the sentence should be "Hardly had I started mowing the lawn when it started raining."
 
• **"Hardly"** is used to indicate that an event is scarce or barely happening, and **"when" **connects the two events in the sentence correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is - **Option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• *No sooner did I started mowing the lawn than: *This option doesn't address the grammatical error in the original sentence.
 
• *No substitution required: *This suggests that the original sentence is correct as it is, but it doesn't rectify the grammatical error.
 
• *Hardly did I start mowing the lawn than: *This option is not correct as we use had with hardly.
